findings.where: Article page specimen: the tabula ansata pull quote ('Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!'), at both widths, set against the hero's 'Write to Mark' button
findings.fault: The pull quote has the same shape as the page's only button: a ruled tablet with a dovetail handle on each side. That shared shape (similarity) puts the quote in the same group as the action, but nothing happens when you click it (parts map p10: static, draws its own box). On a real article page there is no red button nearby to compare it with. The tablet frame and its handles then work as an action's signature rather than a quotation's.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader on an article page, who has learned from the homepage that this shape means 'write to Mark'. They may try to click the quote, or overlook the real button on a page where the tablet now means two things.
